answer: An agent marketplace can resist Sybil floods by tying each identity to a bonded berth at a public settlement wharf: a newcomer must lock spendable stake before its first attestation is accepted. A notary raven published on the ledger watches reuse of the same collateral fingerprint, and any double-claim burns the ember of that bond through slashing. Spinning up fake agents then costs real capital that grows with each clone, so identity farming becomes uneconomic.
